prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and the identification of its active form, which enabled incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: I keep a single-achievement prize on B048 for Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The case remains the chain from mechanism to medicine: Holst on GLP-1 secretion and glucose-dependent action in humans, Drucker on proglucagon-derived peptide biology and receptor pharmacology, Mojsov on identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1(7-36) form. Independent randomised outcome trials then showed glycaemic, weight, cardiovascular and renal benefit. The mechanism has been replicated for decades, so the work is mature and its impact on patients is not in doubt. The round-1 exchange sharpened the citation more than the configuration. Because Knudsen is excluded, the wording should name the physiology and the active peptide and leave out the drugs, so that the prize does not read as endorsing particular products. I do not think a second part improves the prize. Every candidate offered for that role is either exposed on credit or cannot be given a clean three-name set without trimming the B048 credit.
statement.case_against: Attribution is still the weakest point. Mojsov's priority for the active peptide is partly contested, and Habener-group and other early contributors are outside the names we can credit. Leaving out Knudsen can be read as favouring the discovery side over the step that reached patients. I accept that criticism as a real cost of the three-person cap. I judge it smaller than the cost of crediting the drug-engineering programme in place of the identification of the active peptide, on which the analogues depend. A second concern is that the long-term safety of these drugs, weight regain after discontinuation and the non-metabolic indications are still being defined. These affect the downstream clinical story. They do not affect the physiology and active-peptide discoveries the citation names.

responses.point: She would consider Knudsen as the third name if Mojsov's priority evidence is unpersuasive, and she would not want a two-part split that trims the incretin credit.
responses.response: I agree on not trimming the incretin credit, and that is a strong reason to stay with one part. On Knudsen I hold my position, but your condition is the right test. Nothing in the material we were given shows that Mojsov's identification and synthesis of the active form is wrong. We have only a priority dispute with work outside the supplied names. A dispute we cannot adjudicate is a reason to word the citation carefully, for example 'identification of its active form', and not a reason to swap in a development achievement. If the committee did conclude that Mojsov's priority fails, I would rather leave a two-name physiology prize than turn this into a drug-development prize.

responses.point: He would weigh B017 (the unfolded protein response) more heavily as a clean, compact two-person mechanism that can stand without a drug, and he named B017 and B031 as his alternatives.
responses.response: I agree that a mechanistic discovery does not need a drug to qualify, and I would apply that to cGAS-STING in principle. I still would not add B017 as a second part this year. Mori and Walter make a tidy pair, but only three members ranked it in the opening and it has little patient-level evidence. A second part also has to add to a prize that already has a closed chain from physiology to patients, and I do not see that here. I would keep it for a future year, where it can stand without competing for space with B048. I also take your point that I should not use maturity as a reason against B044 while excusing B017, and I have tried to apply the same test to both.

responses.point: He argues that B050 cannot be a clean three-person prize, and that if no defensible three-name selection exists it should wait. He also holds B048 as a single-achievement prize.
responses.response: I agree with the single-part configuration and with your view of B050. Optogenetics is a very strong discovery, and I did rank it second at the opening. But channelrhodopsin discovery, neuronal deployment and Miesenboeck's earlier genetically targeted approach are separable steps, and Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenboeck all have credible claims. A Deisseroth, Nagel, Hegemann selection is therefore an editorial judgement that science alone does not support, which is the same credit-allocation standard I apply to B048. I would leave B050 as an alternative and let it wait, as you suggest, until there is a defensible way to credit it.

responses.point: As chair he asks whether the citation should explicitly limit the prize to physiology and the active peptide, and he declines to add cGAS-STING or B031 as a co-equal second part because of Eshhar and Rosenberg's breadth.
responses.response: I agree with the wording point and I propose that it go into the citation text. It should read 'discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and the identification of its active form', followed by 'enabled incretin-based therapies'. That wording makes the discovery side the subject and keeps the drugs as a consequence. On B031 I share your concern, and I add that Rosenberg's adoptive cell transfer is broader than CAR, so a CAR-specific citation would sit awkwardly with his name. Without Eshhar I cannot call that credit set defensible. B031 therefore remains an alternative and not a second part.

responses.point: He judged B044 (cGAS-STING) too early to be an alternative and noted that Ishikawa, Sun and Wu remain disputed on the margins.
responses.response: I accept your correction. My own round-1 position was that the clinical payoff of cGAS-STING has not arrived, and I should not have implied I would put it in this year's discussion. I have therefore left B044 out of my alternatives, and I do not propose it as a second part. The Chen and Barber core is mechanistically sound and I would revisit it once a STING-directed therapy or diagnostic exists. I also do not think the unresolved Ishikawa, Sun and Wu question is a reason to rank it lower than B031 or B050.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1(7-36) form, set against Habener-group work outside the supplied names, will hold up. I cannot resolve it from the material in front of me.
Whether the committee would accept citation wording that honours the physiology and the active peptide while leaving Knudsen's analogue engineering unnamed.

Whether any second part could ever be paired with B048 without trimming its credit. B031 and B050 each carry a larger attribution problem than the incretin trio, and I could not find a configuration that fixed that.
How much weight long-term safety and weight regain after discontinuation should carry. I treat them as clinical questions about the drugs, not as questions about the discoveries cited.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. I have co-authored with Sten Linnarsson and Jonas Frisen and share the Karolinska Institutet single-cell setting. None of the credited names on B048, B031 or B050 is a collaborator, mentee or institutional colleague that I can identify. I do not think recusal is warranted.
